SM18L-B1.note: Cold solve: 40 sq yd = 360 sq ft; 0.35*360=126; +60 = 186. 666 is struck without real work: 0.35*360 < 0.35*400 = 140 so the total cannot reach 200 (and 666-60=606 is not a multiple of 14 = 0.35*40, though that residue is not cheaper than solving). The 'square the conversion' step is a memorised trap, not an insight; a strong student does this routinely. This is a PSDA units item, not Algebra. Repair: replace 666 with an under-200 distractor; reclassify domain or accept as medium.

SM18L-B2.note: Cold solve: add -> x+y=4; subtract -> x-y=2.5; product 10. Verified x=3.25, y=0.75 satisfies both. Free strike: 40 is the printed 25+15 (constant echo). 6.25 is the lone non-integer and is a distractor - not a per-item strike but the same pattern recurs in B7. The factoring insight is real but fully bypassed on the digital SAT: Desmos gives the intersection (3.25, 0.75) in seconds and x^2-y^2 follows; ordinary elimination is under a minute. Repair: replace 6.25 with an integer distractor (e.g. 16 = (x+y)^2).

SM18L-B3.note: Cold solve: slope 2/3; (14-2k)/(2k-4)=2/3 -> 42-6k=4k-8 -> k=5; points (5,10),(11,14) check. All three distractor derivations reproduce (17 from slope -2/3, 3 from slope 4, -8 from -3/2). No no-arithmetic strike, but back-solving is cheap: plug k=5 first gives (5,10),(11,14), slope 4/6, done; k=17 and k=-8 both give y falling as x rises, killed by sign alone. No insight step - rewrite slope, equate, solve. Standard medium parameter item.

SM18L-B4.note: Cold solve: 24+54=78 at 500 kWh; 105-78=27; 27/0.25=108; 608. Distractors reproduce. No option can be struck with no arithmetic, BUT the decision point the subskill names ('identify the tier') is given away by the option set: all four options exceed 500, so the student is told they are in tier 3 before doing anything. What remains is subtract-and-divide. Second structural tell: every distractor is a 'forgot to subtract a subtotal' overshoot, so the key is the minimum option; 704 and 824 are the same error family (author's own flag) and cannot both be live. Repair: replace 704 (or 824) with a sub-500 distractor such as 450 (81/0.18, tier-2 without adding back 200) or 420 (105/0.25), which restores the tier decision and moves the key off the minimum.

SM18L-B5.note: Recounted cold: (2x-5)/(x+3) > 1 <=> (x-8)/(x+3) > 0 <=> x<-3 or x>8. In [-12,12]: -12..-4 = 9, 9..12 = 4, total 13; x=-3 undefined, x=8 gives exactly 1 (excluded). Key 13 confirmed. Distractor counts reproduce (4; -2..7 = 10; -12..7 minus -3 = 19). No no-arithmetic strike. The case split / sign chart is a real decision point; the only bypass is graphing in Desmos and counting 13 lattice points, which is slow and error-prone rather than routine. Concern is fit, not difficulty: rational inequalities are not in the SAT Algebra (linear) domain and are not really on the SAT at all; this reads as Algebra 2 / competition. Hard, but off-blueprint - gate should decide whether it belongs in this domain.

SM18L-B6.note: Recounted cold and by brute force over k in [-200,200]: x = 4 + 30/(k-3); k-3 must divide 30 and x>0. Positive divisors give 8 (x = 34,19,14,10,9,7,6,5); negative divisors need 30/d > -4 i.e. d in {-10,-15,-30} giving x = 1,2,3 (k = -7,-12,-27). Total 11 confirmed; k=3 has no solution. Distractor stories reproduce (6 = tau(18), 8 = positive divisors only, 13 = 8 + the five wrong negative divisors). No free strike: all options sit inside the only cheap bound (<= 16 signed divisors). Genuinely hard - the rewrite to 4 + 30/(k-3), the divisor step, and the x>0 sign case are three separate decision points, and there is no Desmos or back-solve bypass. Fit concern: divisor counting for integer solutions is number theory, not SAT Algebra; the real SAT never asks this. Hard, off-blueprint.

SM18L-B7.note: Cold solve: y=7-x into 3x+2y=16 gives x=2, y=5; 2a-10=6, a=8. a=-3 (parallel) is not offered so 'exactly one solution' is decoration. Distractor derivations reproduce. No no-arithmetic strike, but 5.5 is the lone non-integer distractor (second instance after B2) and the key is the maximum option with no overshoot distractor (author concedes). This is the standard concurrent-lines procedure with no insight; the author concedes it. Medium. Repair: replace 5.5 with an overshoot integer such as 11 (forgetting to subtract 3 in (3+a)x=22 with x=2).
